summary: The candidate is test-only hardening for a production fix already present in the recorded base through upstream PR #37441. FLUX.2 still excludes SAGE_ATTN from its automatic-selection preference set, but the base selector admits an explicitly requested SAGE_ATTN after platform resolution and semantic capability validation. Restoring the pre-#37441 strict membership condition reproduces the original whitelist failure exactly; the exact candidate regression passes on the prepared base and adds useful FLUX.2-specific coverage without changing production or native code.

tests.what_was_measured: Prepared-base selector suite: 25 tests and 4 subtests passed, confirming the pre-existing explicit-backend capability-admission behavior before applying the candidate.

tests.command: Temporarily restore the pre-#37441 strict model-set membership condition, then run pytest -q ... -k flux2_explicit_sage_backend_bypasses
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction. The candidate regression failed with the original error: Attention backend 'sage_attn' is not supported by this attention layer; supported backends: ['aiter', 'aiter_sage', 'fa', 'torch_sdpa']. The exact candidate source was restored afterward and verified clean.
All three candidate FLUX.2 cases passed: explicit SAGE_ATTN bypasses the automatic-selection set, implicit selection respects it, and missing packed-varlen capability fails closed.
Complete candidate selector suite: 28 tests and 4 subtests passed.

tests.command: Independent fake-platform adversarial probe for FLUX.2 component override, explicit per-call selection, and packed-varlen rejection
tests.what_was_measured: Both component-specific and per-call explicit SAGE_ATTN requests bypassed the FLUX.2 automatic-selection set, while an unsupported packed-varlen requirement still raised ValueError.

The host was identified as AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950, ROCm 7.2. The real resolver raised 'SAGE_ATTN is not supported on rocm', confirming that no SageAttention execution claim can be made on this architecture.

tests.command: git diff --exit-code a0905d0fad4c0d6756bdbfc02ecf66dfd03a579b after temporary failing-before edit
tests.what_was_measured: The exact candidate checkout was restored byte-for-byte before returning to the prepared review branch.

gpu_execution_evidence: Torch detected the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X as gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- under ROCm 7.2, but the production ROCm resolver rejects SAGE_ATTN. No SageAttention kernel or FLUX.2 model was executed.
remaining_limitations: The assigned architecture is AMD gfx950 rather than NVIDIA Blackwell sm_120, and sageattention is not installed in the prepared interpreter; the CUDA resolver and SageAttention kernel path were not executed.
FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv weights were unavailable, so full model construction, serving startup, image generation, and semantic accuracy were not tested.
The candidate changes only Python tests. It contains no production or native-code changes, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The conclusion fully resolves the original whitelist-selection contract at source/selector level; it does not independently qualify SageAttention numerical correctness or FLUX.2 image quality.
